claim: Most proteins can reach their native structure spontaneously in vitro.
source: Even though in vitro most proteins can reach their native structure spontaneously (Anfinsen, 1973), this is not always the case in cellular conditions and proteins can populate misfolded states which can form cytotoxic aggregates (Dobson, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Anfinsen, 1973

claim: Proteins can populate misfolded states which can form cytotoxic aggregates in cellular conditions.

claim: Cells employ specialized proteins called molecular chaperones to counteract misfolding and aggregation.
source: In order to counteract misfolding and aggregation, cells employ specialized proteins, called molecular chaperones, which act on non-native protein substrates by processes that stringently depend on ATP hydrolysis for most chaperone families (Hartl, 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hartl, 1996

claim: Molecular chaperone processes stringently depend on ATP hydrolysis for most chaperone families.
source: In order to counteract misfolding and aggregation, cells employ specialized proteins, called molecular chaperones, which act on non-native protein substrates by processes that stringently depend on ATP hydrolysis for most chaperone families (Hartl, 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hartl, 1996

claim: Hsp70s assist a plethora of fundamental cellular processes beyond prevention of aggregation.
source: Among them, the ubiquitous 70 kDa heat-shock proteins (Hsp70s) play a special role because they assist a plethora of fundamental cellular processes beyond prevention of aggregation (Clerico et al., 2019; Rosenzweig et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Clerico et al., 2019 and Rosenzweig et al., 2019

claim: Hsp70s consist of two domains: the substrate binding domain (SBD) and the nucleotide binding domain (NBD).
source: Hsp70s consist of two domains: the substrate binding domain (SBD) interacts with disparate substrate proteins, whereas the nucleotide binding domain (NBD) is responsible for the binding and hydrolysis of ATP.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayer, 2013 in the preceding sentence

claim: The substrate binding domain (SBD) interacts with disparate substrate proteins.
source: Hsp70s consist of two domains: the substrate binding domain (SBD) interacts with disparate substrate proteins, whereas the nucleotide binding domain (NBD) is responsible for the binding and hydrolysis of ATP.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayer, 2013 in the preceding sentence

claim: The nucleotide binding domain (NBD) is responsible for the binding and hydrolysis of ATP.

claim: The two domains of Hsp70 are allosterically coupled.
source: The two domains are allosterically coupled, and the nature of the nucleotide bound to the NBD affects the structure of the SBD and as a consequence the affinity for the substrate and its association/dissociation rates.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayer, 2013 in the preceding context

claim: When the chaperone is in the ATP-bound state, the SBD is open and easily accessible to the substrate.
source: More precisely, when the chaperone is in the ATP-bound state, the SBD is open and easily accessible to the substrate, whereas the SBD is closed when ADP is bound.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayer, 2013 in the preceding context

claim: The SBD is closed when ADP is bound to Hsp70.
source: More precisely, when the chaperone is in the ATP-bound state, the SBD is open and easily accessible to the substrate, whereas the SBD is closed when ADP is bound.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayer, 2013 in the preceding context

claim: Substrate binding and unbinding rates when ATP is bound are orders of magnitude faster than when ADP is bound.
source: These structural differences result in substrate binding and unbinding rates when ATP is bound that are orders of magnitude faster than when ADP is bound (Mayer et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayer et al., 2000

claim: The substrate, together with a co-localized J-domain protein (JDP), greatly accelerates the hydrolysis of ATP.
source: Furthermore, the coupling is bidirectional: the substrate, together with a co-localized J-domain protein (JDP) that serves as cochaperone (Kampinga and Craig, 2010; Kampinga et al., 2019), greatly accelerates the hydrolysis of ATP.
evidence: Supported by citations to Kampinga and Craig, 2010 and Kampinga et al., 2019

claim: J-domain protein (JDP) serves as cochaperone.

claim: Non-equilibrium affinity (ultra-affinity) can be enhanced beyond the maximum limit allowed by thermodynamic equilibrium.
source: Substrate binding thus benefits from the fast association rate of the ATP-bound state and the slow dissociation rate of the ADP-bound state, resulting in a non-equilibrium affinity (ultra-affinity) that can be enhanced beyond the maximum limit allowed by thermodynamic equilibrium, namely the affinity of the ADP-bound state (De Los Rios and Barducci, 2014; Barducci and De Los Rios, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to De Los Rios and Barducci, 2014 and Barducci and De Los Rios, 2015

claim: Binding of Hsp70 increases the sensitivity of misfolded Luciferase to proteolysis.
source: Biochemical assays revealed that binding of Hsp70 increases the sensitivity of misfolded Luciferase to proteolysis and decreases its propensity to bind Thioflavin-T, strongly suggesting a loss of compactness (Sharma et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sharma et al., 2010

claim: Hsp70s destabilize the tertiary structure of several different substrates.

claim: Six binding sites on the rhodanese sequence were identified using two distinct bioinformatic algorithms.

claim: Chaperone binding leads to larger radii of gyration and higher potential energies.

evidence: Supported by citation to Kellner et al., 2014 and data shown in Figure 1

Each site can be either free or occupied by an ADP- or ATP-bound chaperone for a total of 36 = 729 different states.

claim: Hsp70 chaperones crucially contribute in vivo to the solubility and functionality of a sizeable fraction of the E. coli proteome that would otherwise spontaneously misfold and aggregate.

claim: The ability of chaperones to favor native states might have partially relieved the selection pressure for strong equilibrium thermodynamic stability.
source: Likewise, they raise fundamental questions about the evolution of protein sequences: indeed, since chaperones are ubiquitous and very much conserved across the different kingdoms of life, their ability to favor native states might have partially relieved the selection pressure for strong equilibrium thermodynamic stability, thus allowing evolution to proceed faster and to be more tolerant for slightly destabilizing mutations, as suggested in Rutherford and Lindquist (1998); Tokuriki and Tawfik (2009).
evidence: Speculative interpretation supported by citations to Rutherford and Lindquist, 1998 and Tokuriki and Tawfik, 2009

claim: Hsp70s play a fundamental role in protein translocation, protein translation, and disassembly of protein complexes.
source: Besides the unfolding of non-native substrates discussed in this work, Hsp70s are highly versatile machines that play a fundamental role in a variety of diverse cellular functions such as protein translocation, protein translation, and disassembly of protein complexes.
evidence: Draws from established scientific knowledge

claim: In all Hsp70 processes, Hsp70 binding to flexible substrates in constrained environments requires the energy of ATP hydrolysis (ultra-affinity) and results in the generation of effective forces due to excluded volume effects (entropic pulling).
source: All these processes share basic analogies from the mechanistic point of view: in all these cases, Hsp70 binding to flexible substrates in constrained environments requires the energy of ATP hydrolysis (ultra-affinity) and results in the generation of effective forces due to excluded volume effects (entropic pulling), which ultimately drive protein translocation into mitochondria (De Los Rios et al., 2006; Assenza et al., 2015), clathrin cage disassembly (Sousa et al., 2016) and/or prevention of ribosome stalling (Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to De Los Rios et al., 2006, Assenza et al., 2015, Sousa et al., 2016, and Liu et al., 2013

claim: The force-generating mechanism of Hsp70 chaperones does not rely on any power-stroke conformational change but rather depends on the efficient conversion of ATP chemical energy into ultra-affinity.
source: This mechanism does not rely on any power-stroke conformational change but it rather depends on the efficient conversion of ATP chemical energy into ultra-affinity.
